procedure: State: The same reproducibly failing configuration has valid removable elements and the resettable repeatable task test. Procedure: Run failure-preserving reduction trials: in fixed identifier order try each valid one-element deletion, retain a deletion only when failure recurs, restart from the retained reduced configuration, and stop after a complete pass accepts no deletion or the 80-test budget is exhausted. Limits and stopping conditions: Do not assume monotonicity, treat unresolved as failure, or generalize beyond valid deletions and this task; multiple minimal subsets can exist.
action: Run failure-preserving reduction trials: in fixed identifier order try each valid one-element deletion, retain a deletion only when failure recurs, restart from the retained reduced configuration, and stop after a complete pass accepts no deletion or the 80-test budget is exhausted.
observables: Which reduced configurations still fail, which pass and which are unresolved.
inferential_warrant: The retained subset reproduces failure. A completed final pass establishes one-deletion minimality among valid deletions under this repeatable task test; a budget stop supports only a reduced sufficient subset. This exposes test-relative interactions, not global necessity or a unique cause.
problem_decomposition: Replace feature-by-feature priority as the explanatory unit with the retained failure-preserving subset and its tested deletion boundary.
next_inquiry: The next trial is the next valid deletion from the currently retained failure case; ordinary follow-up examines its observed interaction after the reduction ends.
